titulo: What Happens If You Stop Sleeping? The 11-Day Record #shorts
premisa: A documentary-style story told in two layers. Narration puts YOU in the chair ('By hour 24, you...'), then cuts to what was really happening to Randy Gardner, a 17-year-old San Diego high schooler who stayed awake 264 hours (about 11 days) from December 28, 1963 to January 8, 1964 for a science fair project. His friends Bruce McAllister and Joe Marciano kept him awake, and Stanford sleep researcher William Dement later joined them. Escalation: at 24 hours your reaction time is about as bad as being legally drunk, with a blood alcohol level around 0.10%. At 48 hours your brain starts stealing 'microsleeps', blackouts lasting seconds while your eyes are open. By about 72 hours your mood swings, your memory slips and the world starts to look wrong. Randy grew moody and forgetful, his speech slurred and he hallucinated, mistaking a street sign for a person. Around day 4 he became convinced he was Paul Lowe, a running back for the San Diego Chargers. On day 11 he held a press conference, then slept about 14 hours and 40 minutes and woke up seemingly fine. No version of this story is a countdown list: the hours only mark the turning points in Randy's story.
gancho: What happens to your body if you just... stop sleeping? In 1964, a 17-year-old kid tried it for 11 days straight.
